title: Constant scalar quotient sheaf is a cokernel
statement: Let C be a site with objects in Type(u+1), morphisms in Type(u), and essentially small in Type(u+1). Let J be its topology, A a commutative ring in Type(u+1), and r in A. In the category of sheaves of A-modules on J, the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] with value A/(r) is canonically isomorphic to the cokernel of multiplication by r on the tensor unit sheaf.

source.place: The field-tensor argument and finite scalar filtration, abstracted to the categorical hypotheses; see also Stacks more-algebra.tex, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent (Tag 0H75).

proof.text: In A-modules the range of multiplication by r on A is the principal ideal (r), so the quotient-to-range comparison identifies A/(r) with its cokernel. The constant presheaf functor preserves finite colimits because these are objectwise, and sheafification preserves them as a left adjoint. Apply the resulting constant sheaf functor to this cokernel. Its linearity identifies the resulting endomorphism with r times the identity. Finally the strong monoidal unit comparison of sheafification identifies the constant A sheaf with the tensor unit.

proof_origin.place: Existing proved declaration CategoryTheory.Sheaf.constantSheafQuotientIsoCokernel; its complete implemented proof was read, reused unchanged, and summarized in the steps.
